title: Lawn Round Log

candidates.name: Lawn Round Log
candidates.why: Names the specific job - a mower's round kept as a log - rather than a category, and it is three plain words with one canonical spelling, so the radio test is perfect; it gives up a little distinctiveness and trademark headroom because 'Lawn ... Log' is descriptive and unownable.

candidates.name: Kerbside: Lawn Round Log
candidates.why: An ownable two-syllable roadside carrier plus the full job phrase, but 'kerb' is the UK spelling of 'curb' and reads as a misspelling to the en-US default audience, which fails the radio test on the primary locale.

candidates.name: Mowpath: Lawn Round Log
candidates.why: The carrier is short, pronounceable and stands apart from the incumbent titles, but 'Mowpath' is an invented token with no user phrasing behind it and its Play and trademark field could not be cleared in this session.

candidates.name: Round Ledger
candidates.why: A memorable and ownable pairing, but it drops the domain word 'lawn' that a mower actually types, and 'ledger' narrows the app to money when the job is visits and order as well as balances.

candidates.name: Mowbook: Lawn Round Log
candidates.why: It carries the full job phrase, but the measured shelf already ships Yardbook and LawnBook, so a -book carrier does not stand apart from the top incumbents - it is a one-word swap from an existing title, which is rejection 16.

candidates.name: Swath
candidates.why: A vivid mown-strip metaphor with high distinctiveness, but it fails the radio test on the swath/swathe spelling ambiguity and names a strip of cut grass rather than the round, so it teaches nothing searchable.

candidates.name: Lawn Tracker
candidates.why: It carries the head term, but it is the measured incumbent com.lawntracker.app's exact title and the shelf's generic shape, so it spends the strongest ranking field on a phrase the leaders already own.

candidates.name: Rounds
candidates.why: Evocative of the job in one word, but with no word a mower types it cannot be found in Play search and it does not say what is done with the round.

candidates.name: Tracker
candidates.why: The bare category noun used as the negative control: it spends Play's strongest ranking field on the head term the category leader owns and gives a user nothing to prefer.

rejected.name: Mowbook: Lawn Round Log
rejected.reason: A -book carrier on a shelf that already ships Yardbook and LawnBook is one word swapped from the measured incumbent com.lawnbook.app (LawnBook - Smart Lawn Care), which is rejection 16; the collision hard check outranks its 71.

rejected.name: Mowpath: Lawn Round Log
rejected.reason: The carrier is an invented token with no measured user phrasing behind it and its Play and trademark collision could not be cleared in this session, and it is opaque to a ru reader; an uncleared hard check outranks its 79.

rejected.name: Kerbside: Lawn Round Log
rejected.reason: 'Kerb' is the UK spelling of 'curb' and reads as a misspelling to the en-US default audience, so it fails the radio test and rejection 11 (more than one plausible spelling) despite scoring 79.

rejected.name: Round Ledger
rejected.reason: It drops 'lawn', the domain word a mower types into search, and 'ledger' describes only the money half of a job that is visits, order and balances.

rejected.name: Swath
rejected.reason: It fails the radio test on swath/swathe and names a strip of cut grass rather than the round, so it is neither findable nor specific to the job.

rejected.name: Lawn Tracker
rejected.reason: It is the exact title of the measured incumbent com.lawntracker.app and the shelf's generic head-term shape, so it competes for a phrase the leaders already own (rejections 6 and 14).

rejected.name: Rounds
rejected.reason: It is evocative but contains no word a mower types, so it cannot be found in Play search and does not say what the app records.

rejected.name: Tracker
rejected.reason: The bare category noun used as the negative control: it spends the strongest ranking field on the head term the category leader owns and gives the user no reason to prefer this app.

audience: Solo mowers, and the owner of a two-to-three-person mow crew, running 20 to 150 recurring residential or small-commercial customers on a weekly or fortnightly round, who currently keep the round in their head, in a paper notebook, or in a free cloud CRM they half-use.
rationale: The winner is descriptive rather than carrier-plus-job-noun because this slot's paying user is a trade operator who searches in literal phrases and knows no brand: the measured shelf is led by Yardbook, LawnBook, Lawn Tracker and Mowbius, so any carrier here either clones the incumbents' -book and Mow- shapes (rejection 16) or spends an opaque invented token this offline, unmarketed app has no way to teach. "Lawn Round Log" names the specific job a mower does - the round, kept as a log - not the category, which is the distinction the contract draws (a bare category word fails; a phrase about a job passes), and it is the highest-scoring candidate that survives the collision hard checks.
collisionCheck: Web-searched the exact title and close variants on 2026-10-02; no live app titled "Lawn Round Log" surfaced. Nearest shelf titles found: Lawn Care Log (com.orangeforge.lawncarelog, an unrated 10+ install homeowner fertilizer and seeding log - a different job), Lawn Logix (a pro tank-mix calculator), Lawn Care Pro, Lawn Pro and Yard Mastery; the measured operator incumbents are Yardbook, LawnBook, Lawn Tracker, Mowbius and Lawn Love for Providers. A direct Google Play search could not be run from this machine, so this is a web reading rather than a Play-console reading, and a clean search is not trademark clearance.
localisationCheck: The same 14-character Latin string serves both en-US and ru-RU with 16 characters of slack against Play's 30-character cap, so it fits every declared locale with room to spare; it is three plain words using only Latin letters and single spaces (no emoji, ALL CAPS or repeated symbols) with one canonical spelling, and it carries no unfortunate or homophone meaning in ru; the ru listing ships it as a brand-like Latin string rather than a machine translation.
authoringNote: Authored retrospectively on 2026-10-02, after the slot was built and its store pack written. The name "Lawn Round Log" was chosen during the build, before this naming contract existed; this record reconstructs the derivation honestly rather than presenting a decision that was recorded at recon. That ordering is a known defect of this slot, not a property of the name.
